title: Drinking water report and Petersburg system staffing
subtitle: Transit ridership and MobilityPLUS trips, housing-enabling water funding, water tours and newcomer outreach on tap water.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee endorsed the 2023 Drinking Water Summary Report, which is required under the Safe Drinking Water Act, along with the quality management system review and infrastructure maintenance plan update {{vote:m2}}. Staff described strong compliance results, a clean external audit and water system capacity to support growth.

The committee also recommended creating a new full-time Regulatory and Program Assistant position in Water Operations {{vote:m3}}. The position follows a provincial order for the Region to take over treatment at the Petersburg (Knipfel) water system, while the Township of Wilmot handles distribution. Staff said water rates, not the tax levy, will pay for it, and the full cost will appear in the 2025 budget.

The committee also received the Grand River Transit ridership update and the Blue Box transition update for information through the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}. Councillors pressed staff on MobilityPLUS trips that go undelivered. Staff will return in April with an update on booking software. These recommendations go to Regional Council for adoption.

decisions.detail: The committee endorsed the 2023 Drinking Water Summary Report, the Drinking Water Quality Management System review and the infrastructure maintenance plan update, a report required under the Safe Drinking Water Act.
The committee recommended creating a new full-time Regulatory and Program Assistant position in Water Operations to support the Region's takeover of Petersburg water treatment.
The committee received the Blue Box transition update and the Grand River Transit 2023 year-end ridership update for information.

debate: On MobilityPLUS, one councillor noted that the 2023 undelivered trip rate was above the 2.5% target and asked what would change. Staff pointed to a full complement of operators, added capacity approved in the budget, and unallocated hours that can be used during the year.

Staff said MobilityPLUS bookings open seven days ahead and often fill, then cancellations return trips to the pool. Riders may have to call repeatedly, and staff want a way to book once. Staff also want better grouping of trips.

A councillor reported complaints about a lack of printed schedules at the Cambridge terminal. Staff said customers can ask for printed schedules at customer service locations and that staff had been reminded.

On the new water position, councillors asked why it was not a contract role and why it was not in the 2024 budget. Staff said regulatory work has grown with the number of systems and that the provincial order arrived in January, after the budget was prepared.

Councillors asked which projects could qualify for the provincial Housing-Enabling Water Systems fund, which staff described as narrowly defined. Others supported repeat water facility tours and outreach to newcomers on the safety of tap water.
